clue.text: To order cab is essential

indicators.note: putting things to order rearranges them, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: Booking a taxi is a must.
explanation.definitionFit: Something basic is fundamental, the indispensable core of a thing.

clue.text: A blooming comfortable place to be

definitions.text: A blooming comfortable place to be

parts.words: A blooming comfortable place to be
parts.note: blooming sounds like a mild intensifier, but it literally means flowering; the idiom names an easy situation

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an easy, pleasant situation, and literally a garden plot full of flowering shrubs.

clue.text: Disposed to use bar, he vandalises

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A man inclined to swing a metal bar wrecks property.
explanation.definitionFit: A saboteur deliberately damages or destroys equipment or property, a form of vandalism.

clue.text: Paper thrown at union meetings

parts.note: union suggests a trade union, but means marriage; the meetings are weddings

explanation.walkthrough: 'Union meetings' looks like trade-union gatherings with papers hurled in protest; the union is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Small pieces of coloured paper are tossed over a bride and groom at a wedding.

clue.text: Shoe that's in snakeskin

definitions.meaning: a soft leather slip-on shoe of Native American origin
the creature inside the skin is a venomous American water snake of the same name

explanation.surface: A shoe made from reptile leather.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests footwear made of snakeskin; the second reading is the snake itself, which lives inside its own skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a soft slip-on shoe and a venomous North American pit viper.

clue.text: Has a damaging effect on a heavenly body

definitions.meaning: the red planet, fourth from the sun

explanation.surface: Something spoils an attractive person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavenly body' pretends to be a gorgeous figure; it is a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means spoils or impairs, and the noun is the fourth planet of the solar system.

clue.text: Army officer with what may be an excuse for a dog

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
a lie is often offered as an excuse

explanation.surface: A colonel offers a feeble pretext for owning a pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An excuse for a dog' reads as a poor specimen, but 'for' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a sheepdog breed from Scotland and northern England.

clue.text: List, with or without two opening items

definitions.text: List, with or without two opening items

parts.words: List, with or without two opening items
parts.note: the whole word means a roll or list, and dropping its first two letters leaves another word meaning a list

explanation.walkthrough: The word is a list both whole and with its first two letters removed, which leaves ROLL, a register of names.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rolled-up document can hold a list of names or entries.

clue.text: None of it is good, it's said

definitions.text: None of it is good, it's said

parts.words: None of it is good, it's said
parts.note: a twist on the proverb 'no ... is good ...', read as meaning no item of it is good

explanation.walkthrough: 'It's said' points to a proverb, the saying that hearing nothing means all is well.
explanation.definitionFit: Reports of current events; the proverb 'no ... is good ...' is read jokingly as all of it being bad.

clue.text: Ian, bored, that could be carefree

indicators.note: the words say Ian, bored could become something else, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bored man named Ian might turn out to be happy-go-lucky.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes a confident, light-hearted and untroubled manner, close to carefree.

clue.text: Takes in summer visitors

definitions.meaning: to take in food or drink is to gulp it down
migrant birds that arrive in Britain for the summer

explanation.surface: Someone hosts guests during the warm season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer visitors' looks like holidaymakers; it means migratory birds that come to Britain each summer.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means ingests, and the noun names fork-tailed birds that migrate north for summer.

clue.text: One might see flow in this game

parts.words: One might see flow in this
parts.note: read as wordplay, the second half of the answer is a wild arrangement of the letters of flow

explanation.surface: A sport where a current might be spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: WILD (anagram signal) applied to FOWL gives FLOW, so flow is seen in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks, geese and other birds shot for sport are game birds.

clue.text: Overweight boss is a fool

parts.note: overweight means fat
the head is the boss of an organisation, such as a school

explanation.surface: A portly manager turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathead is a colloquial insult for a stupid person, a dimwit.

clue.text: One can't quite make up one's mind to represent the rider

definitions.text: One can't quite make up one's mind

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged so as to stand for, or represent, a new word

explanation.surface: Someone indecisive is chosen to stand in for the jockey.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who dithers wavers and hesitates, unable to reach a decision.

clue.text: One is well rid of it

definitions.text: One is well rid of it

parts.words: One is well rid of it
parts.note: the idiom 'well rid of' means glad to be free of something; read literally, getting rid of sickness makes one well

explanation.definitionFit: Poor physical condition or sickness is what a person sheds on becoming well again.

clue.text: She and Gary disastrously will make bloomers

indicators.note: something going disastrously is thrown into chaos, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A couple's calamitous blunders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' seems to be gaffes or underwear; it means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: These shrubs bear large showy flower heads, so they are things that bloom.

clue.text: Just a footballer playing the game

parts.note: a just, honest person is straight
a forward is an attacking footballer

explanation.surface: Merely a soccer player taking part in a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like 'merely' but means honest. 'Playing the game' is the idiom for acting fairly, not a footballer on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing the game is an idiom for behaving honestly and fairly, which is being frank and above board.

clue.text: Ruddy good fellow, but not Oxbridge material

parts.note: ruddy means red in colour
a brick is old British slang for a reliable, generous person

explanation.surface: A red-faced decent chap who would never get into Oxford or Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: Redbrick universities are the civic universities founded in British industrial cities, contrasted with Oxford and Cambridge (Oxbridge); 'material' puns on their building stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The term describes later British civic universities, distinct from the ancient Oxford and Cambridge colleges.

clue.text: Ample coming from British sailor and German worker

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rating in the British navy
und is the German word for and
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Plenty is supplied by a British seaman and a German labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British' belongs with 'sailor', and 'and' goes with 'German' to give the German for and, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Abundant means plentiful, more than enough, as ample does.

clue.text: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds

definitions.text: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds

parts.words: He doesn't have to be smart to fool the birds
parts.note: smart suggests clever but also well dressed; the figure in the field wears old rags and still deceives crows

explanation.definitionFit: A straw figure dressed in shabby clothes is set up in fields to frighten crows away from crops.

clue.text: Approaching resort of St Malo

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, so the letters of the town's name are reordered

explanation.surface: Nearing the French seaside town of St Malo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town, fitting St Malo, but means sort again.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost and approaching both mean nearly, close to a given amount.

clue.text: I grew agitated about a little pest

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go about, around, the single letter
stirred up and shaken, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone became upset over a small nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns I GREW into ERWIG, and 'about' puts that around A.
explanation.definitionFit: This small insect with pincers is a garden pest that damages plants.

clue.text: The French prohibition on Middle East republic

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the
a prohibition is a ban

explanation.surface: A French-led embargo imposed on a nation in the Middle East.
explanation.definitionFit: The country on the eastern Mediterranean, capital Beirut, is a parliamentary republic in the Middle East.

clue.text: It should make a Mexican less hot-headed

definitions.text: It should make a Mexican less hot-headed

parts.words: It should make a Mexican less hot-headed
parts.note: hot-headed usually means quick-tempered, but here it means having a head heated by the sun, which a broad-brimmed hat shades

explanation.definitionFit: The wide-brimmed Mexican hat keeps the sun off the wearer's head, keeping it cooler.

clue.text: One's among lesser fellows

indicators.note: the letters are found among the words that follow, spanning their join

explanation.surface: Someone counts as one of the lower orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval bonded labourer was one of the lowest class, among inferior men.

clue.text: Does translating into verse

indicators.note: translating changes the word's form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Rendering female deer into poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Odes are lyric poems, so they are pieces of verse.

clue.text: Liable to get broken English with unusual dialect

indicators.note: an unusual form of the word is a rearranged one, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: English spoken in an odd regional variety is likely to be mangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken English' tempts as one phrase, but 'broken' ends the definition and 'English' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate is fragile, easily damaged or shattered.

clue.text: Clothes for soldiers cleaning drains?

definitions.meaning: army working dress, the plain uniform worn for manual duties
menial non-military chores given to soldiers, such as cleaning; the question mark flags this as an example

explanation.surface: Suitable dress for troops sent to unblock sewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drains' could also be a verb meaning tires out, a third sense of the word, but here it names a typical task.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun means both soldiers' work clothing and the menial duties, like cleaning, they do in it.

clue.text: Old aircraft, many of them flown by youngsters

definitions.meaning: slang among older airmen for aeroplanes

definitions.text: many of them flown by youngsters
definitions.meaning: toys of paper or fabric flown on a string by children

explanation.surface: Vintage planes, many piloted by young people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures young pilots; the second sense is children with string-flown toys.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated RAF slang called planes by this name, and children fly the string-held toys in the wind.
